title: Rate limiting and abuse protection middleware
goal: Every API request is rate limited per the CT-PAGE buckets with correct headers, and the auth endpoints get the strict per-IP bucket.
scope_in: Fastify plugin applying buckets: anonymous 30/min/IP, authenticated user 600/min, API key 1200/min, auth endpoints (`/v1/auth/*`) 20/min/IP, usage ingest 60/min/device (route-level), all configurable.
Headers on every response: `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining`, `RateLimit-Reset` (seconds); `Retry-After` and problem body `retry_after_s` on 429.
Client IP extraction behind Fly proxies: `Fly-Client-IP`/`X-Forwarded-For` honoured only up to the configured trusted hop count; IPv6 bucketed by /64.
Route metadata `config: { rateLimit: { bucket: 'default' | 'auth' | 'usage', cost?: number } }` so other lanes declare their bucket.
Failure policy: when Redis is down, fall back to a per-process in-memory limiter at 2x limits for general routes and 1x for the `auth` bucket; never disable limiting silently.
Abuse hook: temporary block (15 min) for IPs exceeding the auth bucket 5 times in 10 minutes.
scope_out: WebSocket frame rate limits (relay lanes; CT-WS-ENVELOPE limits).
build_against: B009 in-memory RateLimitStore with a fake clock and Fastify inject(); a Redis integration test runs when REDIS_URL is set.
interfaces: `rateLimitPlugin: FastifyPluginAsync<{store: RateLimitStore; config: RateLimitConfig; clock?: () => number}>`.
Route config: `{ config: { rateLimit: { bucket: 'default'|'auth'|'usage'; cost?: number } } }`.
Env: `RATELIMIT_*` overrides documented in docs/config via B004 conventions.
acceptance: 31 anonymous requests from one IP in 60 s: the first 30 return 200 with `RateLimit-Remaining` counting down from 29 to 0, the 31st returns 429 with `Retry-After` between 1 and 60 and body `retry_after_s` equal to it.
An authenticated user is limited at 600/min keyed by `usr_` id (not IP): two IPs share one user bucket; an API key is limited at 1200/min by key id.
21 requests in a minute to `POST /v1/auth/token` from one IP: the 21st is 429; requests from another IP are unaffected.
`POST /v1/usage/events` is limited at 60/min per `dev` claim; the 61st returns 429.
A spoofed `X-Forwarded-For` beyond the trusted hop count does not change the bucket key.
With the Redis store throwing, general routes still limit via the in-memory fallback and the auth bucket stays at 20/min; metric `ratelimit_store_errors_total` increments.
`/healthz` and `/readyz` are exempt; `/v1/status` uses the anonymous bucket.
After the window passes (fake clock +60 s) the counter resets.
tests: plugin.test.ts: headers on 200/404/429 and 429 body shape.
buckets.test.ts: per-principal keys and the five default limits.
client-ip.test.ts: proxy chains, spoofed X-Forwarded-For, IPv6 /64.
fallback.test.ts: store errors, auth bucket stays strict.
abuse-block.test.ts and concurrency.test.ts: 15 min block, 100 parallel requests never exceed the limit.
guardrails: MUST count before running handler logic; rejected requests MUST NOT reach DB work beyond principal resolution.
MUST NOT use user-controlled headers for the key unless within the trusted proxy hop count.
MUST return the same 429 body shape for all buckets and MUST NOT leak other users' counters.
MUST NOT fail open without a metric and warning log; the auth bucket MUST NOT fail open to unlimited.
MUST NOT key limits on the raw URL (use the route template) to avoid bypass via path variants.
failure_modes: Redis outage -> degrade as described; recovery switches back automatically within one window.
Missing client IP -> use the socket address; if absent, use a shared `unknown` bucket at the anonymous limit.
Clock skew between instances -> windows computed by the store (Redis Lua/TIME) in production, not the app clock.
